requirements.quote: If an application is no longer interested in the data it is receiving on a stream, it can abort reading the stream and specify an application error code.
requirements.condition: The application is no longer interested in data being received on a stream.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation permits the application to abort reading the stream and specify an application error code.
requirements.why_checkable: An API or runtime test can verify that receiving can be aborted with an application error code under the stated condition.

requirements.quote: If the stream is in the "Recv" or "Size Known" state, the transport SHOULD signal this by sending a STOP_SENDING frame to prompt closure of the stream in the opposite direction.
requirements.condition: The application aborts reading a stream that is in the "Recv" or "Size Known" state.
requirements.required_behavior: The transport should send a STOP_SENDING frame to prompt closure of the opposite stream direction.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can place the stream in either named state, abort reading, and observe whether STOP_SENDING is transmitted.

requirements.quote: This typically indicates that the receiving application is no longer reading data it receives from the stream, but it is not a guarantee that incoming data will be ignored.
requirements.condition: A STOP_SENDING frame has been sent.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation must not treat sending STOP_SENDING as a guarantee that all subsequently incoming stream data will be ignored.
requirements.why_checkable: Implementation logic can be inspected or tested to ensure it does not rely on STOP_SENDING as a guarantee that incoming data is ignored.

requirements.quote: STREAM frames received after sending a STOP_SENDING frame are still counted toward connection and stream flow control, even though these frames can be discarded upon receipt.
requirements.condition: A STREAM frame is received after a STOP_SENDING frame has been sent for the stream.
requirements.required_behavior: The received STREAM frame's data is counted toward both connection-level and stream-level flow control; the frame may then be discarded upon receipt.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The implementation must not omit the frame from connection or stream flow-control accounting merely because STOP_SENDING was sent or the frame is discarded.
requirements.why_checkable: A runtime test can send STREAM frames after STOP_SENDING and inspect both flow-control counters and optional payload disposal.

requirements.quote: An endpoint that receives a STOP_SENDING frame MUST send a RESET_STREAM frame if the stream is in the "Ready" or "Send" state.
requirements.condition: An endpoint receives STOP_SENDING for a stream in the "Ready" or "Send" state.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint sends a RESET_STREAM frame for that stream.
requirements.why_checkable: A protocol test can inject STOP_SENDING in each named state and require an emitted RESET_STREAM frame.

requirements.quote: If the stream is in the "Data Sent" state, the endpoint MAY defer sending the RESET_STREAM frame until the packets containing outstanding data are acknowledged or declared lost.
requirements.condition: An endpoint receives STOP_SENDING while the stream is in the "Data Sent" state and packets contain outstanding stream data.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint may defer RESET_STREAM while the packets containing outstanding data remain neither acknowledged nor declared lost.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: If the endpoint chooses to defer RESET_STREAM under this rule, it must not continue that deferral beyond acknowledgment or loss declaration of the packets containing outstanding data.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet acknowledgment and loss events can be controlled while observing the timing of RESET_STREAM transmission.

requirements.quote: If any outstanding data is declared lost, the endpoint SHOULD send a RESET_STREAM frame instead of retransmitting the data.
requirements.condition: After STOP_SENDING is received, outstanding stream data is declared lost.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint should not retransmit the lost stream data instead of sending RESET_STREAM.
requirements.why_checkable: A loss-recovery test can declare outstanding data lost and distinguish RESET_STREAM transmission from data retransmission.

requirements.quote: An endpoint SHOULD copy the error code from the STOP_SENDING frame to the RESET_STREAM frame it sends, but it can use any application error code.
requirements.condition: An endpoint sends RESET_STREAM in response to STOP_SENDING.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint should copy the STOP_SENDING application error code into RESET_STREAM, though use of another application error code is permitted.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can compare the error codes in an injected STOP_SENDING frame and the resulting RESET_STREAM frame.

requirements.quote: An endpoint that sends a STOP_SENDING frame MAY ignore the error code in any RESET_STREAM frames subsequently received for that stream.
requirements.condition: An endpoint has sent STOP_SENDING and subsequently receives RESET_STREAM for the same stream.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint may ignore the application error code carried by the subsequently received RESET_STREAM frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can supply varying RESET_STREAM error codes after STOP_SENDING and verify that processing does not depend on those codes.

requirements.quote: STOP_SENDING SHOULD only be sent for a stream that has not been reset by the peer.
requirements.condition: An endpoint is deciding whether to send STOP_SENDING for a stream.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint should send STOP_SENDING only if the peer has not reset the stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint should not send STOP_SENDING for a stream already reset by the peer.
requirements.why_checkable: A state-based test can mark a stream as peer-reset and observe whether STOP_SENDING is emitted.

requirements.quote: An endpoint is expected to send another STOP_SENDING frame if a packet containing a previous STOP_SENDING is lost.
requirements.condition: A packet containing a previously sent STOP_SENDING frame is declared lost.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint sends another STOP_SENDING frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A loss-recovery test can declare the carrying packet lost and observe retransmission of STOP_SENDING in a new packet.

requirements.quote: However, once either all stream data or a RESET_STREAM frame has been received for the stream -- that is, the stream is in any state other than "Recv" or "Size Known" -- sending a STOP_SENDING frame is unnecessary.
requirements.condition: All stream data or a RESET_STREAM frame has been received, so the stream is in a state other than "Recv" or "Size Known".
requirements.why_checkable: Although the condition is observable, the statement only calls transmission unnecessary and does not clearly require or forbid it.

requirements.quote: An endpoint that wishes to terminate both directions of a bidirectional stream can terminate one direction by sending a RESET_STREAM frame, and it can encourage prompt termination in the opposite direction by sending a STOP_SENDING frame.
requirements.condition: An endpoint wishes to terminate both directions of a bidirectional stream.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation permits RESET_STREAM to terminate the sending direction and STOP_SENDING to request prompt termination of the opposite direction.
requirements.why_checkable: A bidirectional-stream test can verify that the endpoint supports using the two frame types for their respective directions.
